result.title: StepBench: Diagnosing Real-World Procedural Understanding in AI Agents
result.summary: Evaluating an agent's planning ability remains challenging for open-domain tasks, where verifying procedures through execution is often impractical. Existing evaluations typically assess only the final plan and do not distinguish procedural errors such as missing, incorrect, or misordered actions. We introduce STEPBENCH, a benchmark of 6,885 verified procedures crawled from wikiHow across 81 open-domain categories. From each procedure, we derive 5 diagnostic tasks: four with deterministic answers involving withheld, incorrect, or shuffled steps, and one requiring next-step generation. We additionally evaluate full-plan generation to examine how diagnostic performance correlates with end-to-end plan validity. Using the same procedures across tasks lets us directly compare different planning capabilities. For generation, STEPEVAL identifies critical failures that prevent goal completion. Across 14 configurations of 12 models, we find substantial differences across planning capabilities, with step ordering proving the most difficult: the strongest model correctly orders only 63.0% of procedures, dropping to 33.1% for those with nine or more steps. Incorrect-step detection also predicts judged plan validity across models, suggesting a lower-cost alternative for evaluating generation quality. On STEPBENCH-Val, comprising 214 procedures published in 2026, comprehension scores and rankings remain stable, suggesting limited influence from memorisation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 STEPBENCH，从 wikiHow 采集 6,885 条流程并构造 5 类诊断任务（步骤缺失、错误、乱序的判定与下一步生成），用于区分 agent 规划中不同环节的失败，并比较诊断分数与整体计划有效性的关系。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽不涉及视觉或 latent 状态，但其「按步骤类型拆解过程错误、并以低成本诊断预测端到端有效性」的评价思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中推理轨迹各步贡献与答案正确性的关联，尤其是乱序与长步骤（9 步以上）性能骤降的现象，或与长度泛化/状态更新问题有类比价值。
